source: NCERT Class VII, Our Pasts II, History Ch. 8.

sections.heading: 1. The Crisis of the Mughal Empire
points: After **Aurangzeb (d. 1707)**, weak successors, court factions and financial strain weakened the empire.
**Nadir Shah** of Iran **sacked Delhi (1739)** and carried off huge wealth (incl. the **Peacock Throne** and **Kohinoor**).
**Ahmad Shah Abdali** (Afghan) invaded repeatedly and defeated the Marathas at the **Third Battle of Panipat (1761)**.
Powerful nobles (**Sayyid brothers, Irani and Turani groups**) fought for control at court.

sections.heading: 2. The Successor States (old Mughal provinces)
points: Governors made their provinces **effectively independent** while nominally loyal to the emperor:
These states reformed **revenue collection** (dealt directly with bankers, **ijaradari** = revenue farming) but stayed **suspicious of Mughal officials**.

sections.heading: 3. The New (Rebel) States
points: States that rose in **opposition** to the Mughals:

sub: **Marathas** — founded by **Shivaji**; later led by the **Peshwas** (Poona); expanded across India; levied **chauth (¼ of revenue)** and **sardeshmukhi (⅒)**.
**Sikhs** — organised into the **Khalsa** (by Guru Gobind Singh); later **Maharaja Ranjit Singh** built a kingdom based at **Lahore**.

sections.heading: 4. Watan Jagirs and Warrior States
points: The **Rajputs** (Amber, Jodhpur) held **watan jagirs** (their homelands) and sought to extend control.
Many of these states relied on **local warrior bands, bankers and revenue farmers**.
This fragmentation set the stage for **British (East India Company) expansion**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Nadir Shah sacked Delhi 1739 (took Peacock Throne, Kohinoor); Abdali won Third Battle of Panipat 1761.
Successor states: Hyderabad (Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah), Awadh (Saadat Khan), Bengal (Murshid Quli Khan).
New states: Marathas (Shivaji → Peshwas; chauth ¼, sardeshmukhi ⅒), Sikhs (Khalsa; Ranjit Singh), Jats.
Ijaradari = revenue farming; watan jagir = Rajput homeland assignment.
Fragmentation → opening for the East India Company.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Chauth = ¼** of revenue; **sardeshmukhi = ⅒** — Maratha levies.
**Hyderabad = Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah; Awadh = Saadat Khan; Bengal = Murshid Quli Khan.**
**Nadir Shah (1739)** and **Ahmad Shah Abdali (Panipat 1761)** are different invaders.
Successor states stayed **nominally loyal** to the Mughals; new states rose in **opposition**.
